newsitem.title: USA: Honda expands cleaner-burning Accords to all states.
newsitem.headline: Honda expands cleaner-burning Accords to all states.

text.p: American Honda Motor Co. Inc. said Thursday all of its 1998 Accord LX and EX models with four-cylinder engines will be equipped with low emission technology now required in California.
American Honda, a unit of Honda Motor Co. Ltd., said the move will make it the first automaker to sell a vehicle that meets the California Low Emission Vehicle standard in all 50 states.

Honda said about 240,000 cars, representing about 65 percent of all Accords sold in the United States annually, will feature the cleaner-burning technology. The new Accords are scheduled to go on sale in late September and will be built at the automaker's plant in Marysville, Ohio.

Accords with V-6 engines and the low-priced DX model will not feature the low-emission engines. However, Honda spokesman Art Garner said the automaker plans to eventually expand the programme to other vehicles. Honda's 1996 Civic was the first gasoline-powered car that met California's emission standard.

Honda said the new engines will not cost more and do not sacrifice power and fuel efficiency. The new 2.3-litre engines are capable of 150 horsepower, about 15 percent higher than the previous version, and get 25 to 30 miles to the gallon.
The California standard requires non-methane organic gas emissions to be about 70 percent less than the most stringent federal standard. Those gases are the main ingredient of smog.
